archetype: Azorius flash control whose commander is a converter, not a threat: the table is gifted cards, Heliod, the Warped Eclipse turns those draws into a per-spell discount that lives on the opponents' turns, and the game is won by the second cast of Approach of the Second Sun. deck-audit reads `control` from strategic_frame.json and the slot budget agrees (interaction 14 of 12-15, protection 5 of 5-7, ramp 12 of 10-12, card-advantage 16 of >=10); the conversion is a one-finisher combo deck's, and every count below is read against that.
verdict: The deck survives and does not convert: on the v1.2.1 Forge run it placed second 35 times of 94 ranked games and first 11, won 20 of 99 decided (0.202, ci95 [0.135, 0.292]) against the table's null of 0.181, and every one of the 12 games that reached a second Approach cast won. What limits it is the hub: the back face that makes a seven-drop cast twice affordable existed in 35 of 120 games (0.292, ci95 [0.218, 0.378]) against a goldfish assembly of 0.741, and the five-card protection axis reads AT by count while two of its five do not protect Heliod at all and the only constant piece among them, Lightning Greaves, does nothing against a wrath — in a deck whose own two sweepers destroy him and were cast 70 times in 120 games; the three that do answer removal are single-use instants and a flash creature, and Forge cast two of the three zero times. Protection is the axis that binds; win-condition access (three cards, 0.495) is second; lands and colours are real shortfalls that are not costing the games the evidence can see.

gaps: NO FORGE RUN EXISTS ON v1.3.0. Every table figure here is from run b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, 120 games, standard pod, 2026-09-09) or 4b0e1964 (v1.2.1, 40 games, standard-v3, 2026-09-10); the current list differs by three cards (Isochron Scepter, Horn of Greed, Mind Stone in; Mikaeus, the Lunarch, Forced Fruition, Angelic Wall out) and none of the three has a Forge line. A run on v1.3.0 against standard-v3 at 120+ games is the next measurement; it is not an agent question and no settled_by routes it.

FORGE CANNOT MEASURE THE PROTECTION SUITE. Guardian of Faith: 0 casts, 6 discards in 120 games; Teferi's Protection: 0 casts; interaction_received 0.17 a game (ci95 [0.10, 0.25]) and 0.10 (ci95 [0.01, 0.19]) on the two runs. The AI neither removes Heliod often nor casts the instants that would save him, so the 'protection is adequate' reading in the previous diagnosis was a floor, not a vindication. The evidence that protection binds is the log (entry 001, one game — an anecdote by the charter's rule), the pilot's stated want, and the deck's own 70 wrath casts in 120 games.

THE DISCOUNT IS NOT MODELLED. model-coverage lists Heliod's only channel as bodies; every goldfish mana figure is a floor and no artifact on disk has resolved a single discounted cast. The X-draw-into-Approach line in open_questions is the highest-leverage unknown in the deck.

NO candidate_pool.json AND NO deck_recon.json. Every add above was found with card-search over cards.csv (identity WU, deck's 99 excluded) and checked Commander-legal against the corpus; considering.json on disk is from the Aetherflux Reservoir era and names cards that answer a kill the deck no longer runs — it was read and not used.

SIX CARDS NEVER CAST IN 120 FORGE GAMES, carried from the previous diagnosis: Azorius Signet, Guardian of Faith, Long-Term Plans, Psychosis Crawler, Skyscribing, Teferi's Protection. Skyscribing and Psychosis Crawler are kept here rather than cut on that evidence, because a card the AI declines is not a card that does not help.

THE PILOT'S SECOND WANT — more one-to-three-mana colourless artifacts — is served by two of the nine adds (Mithril Coat {3}, Swiftfoot Boots {2}). Soul-Guide Lantern ({1}, hate:graveyard) was examined and dropped: with Farewell in the prescription the validator shows it moves interaction-breadth not at all (Farewell's 'exile all graveyards' already takes it 3 to 4), so it is the cheaper graveyard answer only if Farewell is not bought. A wider artifact sweep was not run because every add must close a named axis and a generic-cost artifact that closes none is a preference.

THE LAND HALF OF interaction-breadth IS LEFT OPEN. Field of Ruin, Ghost Quarter and Strip Mine are in the pool and would take lands 33 to 34 as well, but the breadth heuristic reads only role-tagged interactive cards and none of the three carries one, so an add that named the axis would fail the validator while doing the thing; and nothing in the two logged games or the two pod runs names a land as the threat.

findings.note: 'Protection is the axis that binds' is stated as the verdict while gaps[1] concedes its evidence is one log game (001, on V5), the pilot's stated want, and '70 wrath casts'. Re-derived from the b0f44e4a logs (sim/logs/...b0f44e4a.../part-0*.log, 120 games parsed): heliod's own Day of Judgment / Supreme Verdict RESOLVED 56 times, Heliod was on the battlefield at 4 of those resolutions, and 5 of Heliod's 50 battlefield exits are attributable to his own wrath (Supreme Verdict 3, Day of Judgment 2). The 70 figure counts casts, not commander losses. The 0.741 -> 0.292 gap the verdict hangs the hub on decomposes, from the record's games[].per_seat.heliod, into 52 of 120 games where Heliod was never cast (commander_casts 0) and 33 of the 68 resolved games where the AI never activated the flip (44 activations total) -- neither is a protection failure -- and engine.json (critic pass, today) says the flip did not move the win rate: 6/35 flip games (0.171) against 14/85 no-flip (0.165), re-derived here from commander_transformed_turn. A hypothesis the pilot holds is worth testing; a verdict needs a measured mechanism, and the one the verdict names is contradicted by the record it cites.

'two of its five do not protect Heliod at all' -- deck-audit's five are Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Kefnet the Mindful, Lightning Greaves, Teferi's Protection (axes[8].measured.cards). Only Kefnet protects nothing but himself. Greaves' shroud stops targeted removal, and in the 120-game logs targeted removal is the commonest thing that took Heliod off the battlefield: Stroke of Midnight 7, Generous Gift 8, Swords to Plowshares 3, Aura Mutation 2, Chaos Mutation 2 = 22 of 50 exits, against 16 to opposing wraths (Farewell 5, Wrath of God 4, Cleansing Nova 3, Hour of Reckoning 2, Austere Command 2) and 5 to the deck's own. Log 001's redirected Swords is exactly the event Greaves prevents. The same sentence then says Greaves 'does nothing against a wrath', which is true and is not 'not at all'.

'The AI neither removes Heliod often' rests on interaction_received 0.17 (ci95 [0.10, 0.25]), a record field. The logs behind that record show Heliod put into graveyard/exile from the battlefield 50 times, in 37 of the 68 games in which he resolved (0.54). Forge measures the THREAT side of protection well; what it cannot show is the response side -- Guardian of Faith 0 casts, Teferi's Protection 0, Karametra's Blessing resolved on Heliod 2 of 9 casts, Greaves attached to Heliod 5 times. The gap should say that, because it changes which protection the evidence asks for: 22 targeted exits favour hexproof/shroud (Boots, Greaves), 21 wrath exits favour indestructible/phasing, and 10 exile exits (Farewell 5, Swords 3, Chaos Mutation 2) answer to neither Coat nor Maneuver.

'The insurance card Forge used most (29 games cast, 41 activations ...)'. engine_casts.by_card counts events, not games (29 casts). Of the 41 Greaves activations the logs show 5 attaching to Heliod (4 'Attach to Heliod, the Radiant Dawn' + 1 Warped Eclipse); the rest went to Thopter tokens and other creatures. As commander insurance Forge used it five times in 120 games. The same figure is reused in add_candidates[0].evidence.forge as 'the Coat is a permanent Forge will equip the way it equipped Greaves 41 times' -- a forecast about the AI stated as evidence. Separately, Mithril Coat's oracle text (cards.csv) carries 'Equip {3}': after a command-zone recast the Coat re-arms for three, which the cited commander-insurance passage ('cheap to re-arm') makes material and the entry omits.

'it satisfies Glacial Fortress and Prairie Stream on entry'. Prairie Stream (cards.csv): 'This land enters tapped unless you control two or more BASIC lands.' Tundra is Land -- Plains Island, not basic, and does not count. Glacial Fortress ('a Plains or an Island') and Flooded Strand ('a Plains or Island card') hold. Note the corpus does not know the pilot's collection: card-search --owned finds Swiftfoot Boots and none of the other ten adds; the charter says ownership is not a criterion, so this is a note, not a finding.

The Mystic Gate drop: 'its coloured mode costs {W/U} on top of the tap, so mana-analysis would file it under sources.gated beside Skycloud Expanse'. Run today: manabase.gated_colour_source(Mystic Gate) returns False (Skycloud Expanse True; Tundra, Sea of Clouds, Adarkar Wastes, Mana Confluence False) and land_colors reads it as {U, W}; mana_analysis.sources.gated on the current list names one card, Skycloud Expanse. The tool the drop is attributed to would count Mystic Gate as an untapped W/U source. Whether a filter land is the right fifth colour source is a different argument, and it is not made.

'Consistency reads 0.868 so this is not what loses games' and the verdict's 'lands and colours are real shortfalls that are not costing the games the evidence can see'. The evidence on disk does see it: record b0f44e4a, 52 of 120 games with commander_casts 0 averaged 7.60 lands against 9.04 in the 68 cast games (recomputed from games[].per_seat; the previous diagnosis carried the Welch diff 1.448, ci95 [0.552, 2.344], and the doctor read that artifact); benchmark.json missed_land_drop_rate 0.2568 with worst turn 6, and land_drop_hit_rate 0.728 / 0.593 / 0.534 across turns four to six (quoted in engine.json stages[0]). Consistency 0.868 is the turn-THREE drop; the finisher costs seven twice. The never-cast half of the 0.741 -> 0.292 gap is the mana-base axis's evidence and the diagnosis leaves it unread.

The 'weakness' verdict at 2 sweepers is cited to strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite, quote 'wipes "one or two max" (Zupke caps at 3)'. Fetched whole, that section says two IS the ceiling, 'the drift is real: the Command Zone template cut wipes 5->3-4 as the format sped up ... so date any wipe count you inherit', and 'wipes out of favour as games speed up'. The 5-7 band is strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's control override ('Bend those there, not here'); the section actually cited argues against the verdict it is attached to. deck-audit's target block carries the same fragment, which is the audit's defect, but the doctor is the reader: cite archetype-selection for the band and say the interaction-suite section disagrees. add_candidates[2] and [7] reuse the fragment to justify +1/+2 wipes.

cost_of_cutting prices Kefnet on the 40-game standard-v3 run ('cast in 14 of 40 games and activated 6 times'; by_card counts 14 casts, not games) and omits the 120-game record the diagnosis uses for every other figure: Kefnet the Mindful cast 39, activated 29 -- the most-cast creature in that run (Drift of Phantasms 35, Archangel of Tithes 28, Consecrated Sphinx 25). 'painful' is the right label; the price is understated by the larger run.

'at six mana it draws one opponent four cards where Prosperity at the same X draws three opponents four each'. Mathemagics at X=2 is {2}{2}{U}{U} = six mana for 2^2 = 4 cards. Prosperity at the SAME X (2) draws each player two for three mana; four each is X=4 at five mana. The conclusion (symmetric X-draw feeds the discount, single-target does not) survives; the sentence does not.

'the six rocks in the flip component are the ones that actually pay {3}{U/P}'. goldfish_targets.json declares six (Arcane Signet, Azorius Signet, Decanter, Sol Ring, Talisman, Thought Vessel); Mind Stone's '{T}: Add {C}' pays the {3} identically and engine.json's proposed_goldfish_edits flags its omission from that any_of. Six is the file's choice, not the deck's; the same slip is in engine.components[1].have.

'Lands plus eight persistent rocks'. deck-audit's persistent_producers list is eight because Smothering Tithe carries ramp:rock (card_roles.json); mana_analysis.sources.producers lists seven rocks and no Tithe. The 41 is the audit's figure and holds; 'eight rocks' is wrong for one, and an enchantment that makes Treasure is not what the Burgess formula counts as a land.

'none puts Approach in hand the turn it is found'. After Mystical Tutor to the top, Temple Bell ({T}), Mikokoro ({2},{T}), Kwain ({T}), Mind Stone ({1},{T}, sac) and Kefnet ({3}{U}) each draw at instant speed the same turn -- five cards in the 99. add_candidates[8] concedes '(or a gift trigger)'. The gap between find and cast is mana in the same window, not a draw step, and Solve the Equation's case should be priced against that.

'the only one that is a land and so survives a Farewell or Austere Command on artifacts'. Enumerated (cards.json, 'no maximum hand size'): Decanter of Endless Water, Reliquary Tower, The Second Doctor, Thought Vessel. The Second Doctor is a creature and survives an artifacts-only mode as well; the Tower is the only one that survives a creatures-plus-artifacts Farewell. Superlative stated one member wider than the set.

'the second-largest single contributor to the number Heliod's discount reads on an opponent's turn' -- no set enumerated and no largest named. Per opponent draw step Font of Mythos (+2) is the largest constant contributor among the eleven gift pieces (Howling Mine, Kami, Dictate +1 each; Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran, Horn are activations or land-gated; Crawler is your upkeep; Doctor your end step). If the largest meant is an X-draw, say so; the 0.574 / 0.537 opener figures are correct (hypergeometric 11 and 10 of 99 in 7).

The Soul-Guide Lantern drop is grounded on validator arithmetic: interaction-breadth is a count of classes, so Farewell alone, Lantern alone and both together all read 4 (audit_mod._interaction_breadth run today on the 99 plus each). That says the axis cannot see a second graveyard answer, not that the deck does not want one. On lean_into[0]'s own argument (buy in the generic-artifact class the discount makes free) a {1} hate:graveyard artifact that also moves the interaction axis 14 -> 15 (Farewell moves it 0: removal:sweeper is not an interaction-axis role) fits the pilot's second want better than a {4}{W}{W} Game Changer sorcery. The gap says 'cheaper graveyard answer only if Farewell is not bought'; it should state the trade, not resolve it by the validator's cap.

All 16 values equal deck-audit run today (33, 41, 2, -11, 12, 16, 14, 2, 5, 3, 16, 3, 0.868, 2, 4, 4). goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json both carry decklist_sha256 f1d4a650...; audit freshness reads current for both. Every goldfish rate quoted (0.921/0.822/2.499, 0.741/0.561/4.87, 0.36, 0.32, 0.787/0.583, 0.839/0.705/3.022, 0.792, 0.495/0.358, 0.683/0.531, 0.68, 0.496/0.357) equals metrics.targets. Enumerated from cards.json: 20 nonland cards with a purely generic cost; four 'no maximum hand size' effects; graveyard mentioned only by Heliod's front face, Dig Through Time, Force of Negation; no card targets a land; Lightning Greaves the only Equipment; five X-draws of which Prosperity and Skyscribing are symmetric; curve 22 two-drops / 18 three-drops / 67 nonland entries / 1 at 8+; 12 roleless entries include Mathemagics.

Fetched with lookup-strategy: ratios, mana-base, mana-base.color-sources, threat-density, archetype-selection, curve, power-level, redundancy-vs-tutors, cutting, multiplayer.commander-insurance, multiplayer.asymmetry, pivot-point -- every quote verbatim and used within its section's meaning. The ratios template is read as the audit's band and explicitly not as what loses games, which respects the section's own 'counts of functions, not cards ... too one size fits all'. Hypergeometric figures 0.574 (11), 0.537 (10), 0.199 (3), 0.137 (2), 31% (5), 7.1% (1) all recompute.

All nine adds are Commander-legal and inside {W,U} (cards.csv). Recomputed with the audit's own counters: Time Wipe and Farewell each take sweepers 2 -> 3 (both removal:sweeper); Mithril Coat, Swiftfoot Boots, Flawless Maneuver each take protection 5 -> 6; Solve the Equation and Personal Tutor each take tutors 4 -> 5 (tutor:narrow); Farewell takes interaction-breadth 3 -> 4 via 'exile all graveyards'. Sea of Clouds is land:tapped in card_roles.json and is untapped with three opponents. bracket_delta 4 -> 4 on all nine is the validator's recompute; Farewell is a ninth Game Changer on a floor already forced by eight. Solve the Equation + Approach is correctly held at 'needs a stack scenario'.

The deck's one passing stack (002, Approach off Mystical Tutor) names none of the seven cuts in its scenario, so orphans_stack [] is right for all seven. Greaves-vs-own-targeting, Time Wipe on a transformed commander, and the X-spell/discount ordering are held as resolve-stack questions rather than asserted; the Greaves swap is explicitly priced on the open answer.

The missing v1.3.0 Forge run is stated accurately: both records carry the v1.2.1 seat sha (214af308...), the three swapped-in cards have no by_card line, and the closed settled_by set (resolve-stack | research-strategy | goldfish) cannot route a simulate, so leaving it in gaps rather than open_questions is the correct shape.

Approach of the Second Sun is the deck's one declared finisher by design (bracket_report combo_content, engine.json wincon stage names it the only SPOF); the diagnosis prescribes ACCESS (tutors to hand) rather than calling the one-finisher shape a defect, which is the right reading of a component that is supposed to be one card.
